title: Bind installed Skills to explicit trusted executors
goal: Ensure a Skill manifest cannot gain access to any registered Module or Tool merely by naming its moduleID or adapter; only explicitly supported Skill IDs with matching module and adapter bindings may execute.
context: Issue #347 remains open for production executor mapping. SkillRuntime.resolveExecutor currently constructs ModuleBackedSkillExecutor for any manifest that declares a non-empty moduleID when ModuleRuntime exists. The executor allowlists adapter strings and checks module IDs for workspace search/read/create, but it does not bind each adapter to its exact Skill ID, and manifests without a chatInputAdapter can pass arbitrary string fields to the named module. This permits an imported or user-edited Skill manifest to try to reuse a registered capability outside the intended Skill identity. Existing ModuleRuntime policy and capability checks must remain intact; explicit registry injection is still a trusted extension point.
forbidden_changes: Do not weaken ModuleRuntime policy, approval, cancellation, capability grants, or schema validation.
Do not allow Skill.md to select arbitrary Swift code, executor types, Module IDs, or adapter names.
Do not remove explicitly injected SkillExecutorRegistry support or the built-in text.normalize executor.
Do not broaden workspace roots, secret filtering, file extension rules, or workspace toggle behavior.
Do not change unrelated UI, provider, storage, terminal, or Xcode project files.
acceptance_criteria: The built-in module-backed bindings are explicit and exact: workspace.search → tool.workspace.read + workspace.search adapter; workspace.read-file → tool.workspace.read + workspace.read-file adapter; workspace.create-file → tool.workspace.write + workspace.create-file adapter.
A manifest with an arbitrary Skill ID cannot execute a built-in workspace adapter even when it copies the matching moduleID and adapter metadata.
A manifest that names a registered moduleID but has no allowlisted adapter fails closed before the module is invoked.
Mismatched Skill ID, module ID, or adapter combinations fail closed and produce no successful verification or mutation.
Explicitly registered custom executors and the built-in text.normalize executor continue to work.
Regression tests prove no unauthorized module invocation occurs for forged manifests and supported M8 Skills still pass end-to-end.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: If a test fails, inspect only SkillRuntime executor resolution, exact manifest/module/adapter bindings, and focused runtime or M8 integration tests. Keep unsupported Skills unavailable, preserve the explicit executor registry, and rerun all required gates.
